title: The River Project That Used Three Kinds of Evidence
passage:
Residents of a town downstream from a forest complained that the river had become muddier after heavy rain. Some blamed recent logging on nearby hills. The forestry company argued that all cutting followed regulations and that storms had simply become more intense. Both sides had photographs supporting their views, but the pictures had been taken on different days and at different places. The town council wanted evidence strong enough to guide action rather than deepen the argument.

A university team proposed using three kinds of information. First, automatic sensors would measure water cloudiness at fixed points every hour. Second, rainfall records would show how much rain had fallen before each change in the river. Third, field teams would inspect several slopes and streams for exposed soil, drainage problems, and erosion. No single source would be treated as sufficient.

The first months produced confusing results. Cloudiness increased after large storms even in areas without recent logging. This supported the company's claim that rainfall mattered. Yet two smaller storms caused unusually muddy water in one branch stream below a newly built forestry road. Field inspection found that a drainage ditch beside the road was sending concentrated runoff toward an unstable slope.

The forestry company repaired the ditch and added barriers to slow the water. During later storms of similar size, cloudiness in that branch stream was lower. The improvement suggested that the road had contributed to at least part of the problem. However, the university team warned against concluding that all river mud had one cause. Other tributaries still became cloudy after intense rainfall because of natural soil movement and older erosion sites.

The town council used the results to change its policy. Instead of debating whether forestry as a whole was ‘the cause,’ it required stronger drainage checks for new roads and additional monitoring after construction. It also began restoring vegetation along two older eroded banks unrelated to current logging.

Some activists felt the council had been too cautious because they wanted stricter limits on tree cutting. Some industry representatives felt the monitoring focused unfairly on forestry. The researchers responded that their task was not to distribute blame equally or choose a political compromise. It was to identify what the evidence could and could not support.

After two years, the river still became muddy during major storms, but several local spikes were reduced. More importantly, the debate changed. Residents, officials, and the company now looked at the same time-stamped data rather than comparing isolated photographs. Disagreement did not disappear, but it became more specific.

The project showed why environmental questions often require multiple kinds of evidence. A sensor can show when water changes but not necessarily why. Rainfall records can reveal patterns but not locate a damaged slope. Field inspection can identify a plausible source but may miss what happens during a storm. When the three sources were combined, the town could move from a broad argument about a whole industry toward targeted actions supported by evidence.
translation:
森林の下流にある町で、大雨後の川が以前より濁るという苦情が出ました。住民の一部は最近の伐採を原因と考え、林業会社は規則を守っており、豪雨が強くなったことが主因だと主張しました。双方に写真はありましたが、撮影日や場所が違い、比較できませんでした。

大学チームは三種類の証拠を組み合わせました。固定地点の濁度センサー、降雨量記録、そして斜面や支流を直接調べる現地調査です。どれか一つだけで結論を出さない方針でした。

最初の数か月では、最近伐採していない地域でも大雨後に濁度が上がり、雨量の影響が大きいことが確認されました。一方、ある新設林道の下流支流では、それほど強くない雨でも異常な濁りが二回発生しました。現地調査すると、道路脇の排水溝が水を一か所へ集め、不安定な斜面へ流していました。

会社が排水路を修理し、水を弱める設備を入れると、同程度の雨でもその支流の濁りは低下しました。林道が問題の一部だった可能性は高まりましたが、研究者は『川全体の濁りがすべて林道原因』とは結論しませんでした。他の支流では、強い雨による自然な土砂移動や古い侵食箇所も影響していたからです。

町は『林業全体が原因かどうか』という議論から離れ、新設林道の排水確認を厳しくし、工事後の監視を増やしました。同時に、現在の伐採とは無関係な古い河岸侵食の修復も始めました。

活動家の一部は伐採規制が弱いと感じ、業界側は林業ばかり調べられると不満を持ちました。研究者は、役割は責任を均等配分することではなく、証拠が何を示し、何を示せないかを明確にすることだと説明しました。

二年後も大雨では川は濁りますが、局地的な急上昇のいくつかは減りました。さらに、議論は単独写真ではなく同じ時刻付きデータを基に行われるようになりました。

この事例は、環境問題に複数の証拠が必要な理由を示します。センサーは変化の時刻を示しても原因までは分からず、雨量記録は傾向を示しても壊れた斜面の場所は特定できません。現地調査も嵐の最中の変化を見逃すことがあります。三つを組み合わせたことで、広い責任論から、証拠に基づく具体的な対策へ進めたのです。
